notes:
**A share-by-email button is no longer reported as a dead mailbox.**

Most sites carry a "share this page by email" link, and the standard way to
write one leaves the recipient blank so the reader can type their own. Docket
read that blank recipient as a published contact address and reported, on every
page carrying the button, that mail sent to it would bounce. It said in the
same sentence that the address was not a valid domain — which is Docket's way
of saying it cannot judge the string, not a finding about your contact details.

**Your logo's alt text is no longer mistaken for your company name.**

A logo described as "Site header logo" was read as a brand called "Site
header", and the report said the company's name appears two different ways.
Docket already ignored "site logo", "header logo" and "main logo"; it now
recognises the pattern rather than the exact phrases.

**Auditing a section still works when the address ends in a file name.**

Point Docket at `example.com/gb/en/` and it spends the crawl on that section.
If the site redirects to `/gb/en/index.html` — or you paste that address
yourself — it now does the same thing. Before, the file name at the end
switched the preference off entirely.
